spots.name: Palazzo dei Priori

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Palazzo dei Priori or comunale is one of the best examples in Italy of a public palace from the communal era. It is located in the central Piazza IV Novembre in Perugia, Umbria. It extends along Corso Vannucci up to Via Boncambi.

spots.name: Perugia Cathedral
spots.summary: Perugia Cathedral, officially the Metropolitan Cathedral of St. Lawrence, is a Roman Catholic cathedral in Perugia, Umbria, central Italy, dedicated to Saint Lawrence.

spots.name: Rocca Paolina

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Rocca Paolina was a Renaissance fortress in Perugia, built between 1540 and 1543 by order of Pope Paul III, based on designs by Antonio da Sangallo the Younger. Its construction entailed the destruction of a significant part of the historic city, including Etruscan, Roman, and medieval structures.

spots.name: Galleria Nazionale dell'Umbria

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Galleria Nazionale dell'Umbria the Italian national paintings collection of Umbria, housed in the Palazzo dei Priori, Perugia, in central Italy.

spots.name: Piazza IV Novembre
spots.summary: Piazza IV Novembre is a square in the historic center of Perugia in Umbria, Italy.

spots.name: San Pietro

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The basilica di San Pietro is a Catholic basilica and abbey in the Italian city of Perugia. Its bell tower, standing at 70 meters tall, is the tallest structure in Perugia and is one of the city's most significant symbols. It is an Italian national monument.

spots.name: Etruscan Well

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Etruscan Well, also known as "Sorbello well" from the name of the noble family which still owns the mansion that is home to the structure, is located in the old town of Perugia. The well is currently open to the public as a museum.

spots.name: San Domenico

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: San Domenico is a Roman Catholic basilica church, located on Piazza Giordano Bruno and via del Castellano in the city of Perugia, region of Umbria, central Italy.

spots.name: San Michele Arcangelo, Perugia

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: San Michele Arcangelo, also known as Sant'Angelo, is a paleo-Christian temple in the city of Perugia in Umbria. The circular building dates to the 5th to 6th century, and incorporates corinthian capped columns from a prior pagan temple.

spots.name: Collegio del Cambio

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Collegio del Cambio is the historic seat of the exchange guild in the Palazzo dei Priori in the city of Perugia, Italy. It was built between 1452 and 1457 and now houses a number of artistic masterpieces.

spots.name: Perusia

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The ancient Perusia, now Perugia, first appears in history as one of the 12 confederate cities of Etruria. It is first mentioned in the account of the war of 310 or 309 BC between the Etruscans and the Roman Republic.

spots.name: Palazzo del Capitano del Popolo

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Palazzo del Capitano del Popolo is a historic building in Perugia, Italy, located in Piazza Giacomo Matteotti, within the Porta San Pietro district. It currently houses the Court of Appeal, the Office of the Attorney General, and various municipal offices.

spots.name: Porta Marzia
spots.summary: This is an Etruscan city gate built in the 3rd century BC and much later incorporated into the city walls. It is close to the remains of the Paolina Fortress.

spots.name: San Severo Chapel

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Houses the only fresco by Raphael that has remained in Perugia.

spots.name: Torre degli Sciri
spots.summary: The Torre degli Sciri, is a medieval tower dating back to the 13th century, located in Perugia, Italy. It stands in the historic district of Porta Santa Susanna, at the beginning of the Via dei Priori. Reaching a height of 42 meters, it is the last complete such tower remaining in the city.

spots.name: Biblioteca Augusta

hours.note: Closed Sat, Sun

spots.summary: The Biblioteca Augusta is a public library in Perugia, Italy, founded by Prospero Podiani. It opened in 1623, housed in the former Palazzo Meniconi on the Piazza Piccola. It currently operates from the Palazzo Conestabile della Staffa in the Porta Sole area of the city.

spots.name: Teatro Morlacchi
spots.summary: Teatro Morlacchi, formerly Teatro del Verzaro, is the largest theater of Perugia. It is named after the musician Francesco Morlacchi.
